name: Chilkoot Trail
region: Chilkoot Trail National Historic Site, British Columbia and Alaska
why: The route of the Klondike gold rush of 1898, from the Alaskan coast over the Chilkoot Pass to Lake Bennett, past the rusting gear left by the stampeders.
book: Permit for the Canadian side from Parks Canada (1 June to mid-September), compulsory in-person orientation at the Skagway Trail Center. Back from Bennett by the White Pass and Yukon Route train or a float plane. Passport needed: the trail crosses the border.
water: Rivers and lakes; treat all water.
dangers: The Scales and the pass: boulder fields in fog and snow, even in July.
Black and grizzly bears: food lockers at camps.
Avalanche slopes above the trail until late June.
turnaround: Cross the pass early in the morning: storms build up later.
